title: Success Here = Success There
description: This week, we visit the fabric survival equipment shop to see how Team Robins is ensuring the safety of F-15 pilots downrange! (U.S. Air Force video by Paul Wenzel)
keywords: Robins Air Force Base, Ejection Seat, F-15, parachute

transcript.text: Hey Team Robbins, today we're here at the Fabric Survival Equipment Shop.
Let's go see what they do.
The Robbins Fabric Survival Equipment Shop not only has a mission of creating floor blankets,
curtains, and cargo nets for various weapon systems and inspecting aircraft survival kits,
but also has a task of inspecting and assembling parachutes which sit on top of F-15 ejection
seats.
It's a delicate tedious task for parachute packers.
A room dedicated for the operation includes several 20-plus foot tables which each parachute
is inspected.
Parts are replaced as needed and repacked for return to a waiting fighter aircraft.
Currently, the parachute shop is expecting a high volume of parachutes to be inspected,
a total of 17 from mid-October to early noon.
To meet the goal, the shop enlisted the assistance of longtime parachute packer Master Sergeant Kevin
Spano, Air Force Reserve Command.
The service life of a parachute is 13 years and is inspected each time an F-15 arrives
at Robbins for program depot maintenance.
From Robbins Air Force Base, I'm Terre McGross.
Airman of Robbins Air Force Base.
To me, you're an airman.
Whether you're a wear the uniform, whether you're a civil servant, or whether you're one
of our commercial partners, you're an airman engaged in delivering combat power every
day.
And remember, success here equals success there.
Thank you.
